newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas prices soften on moderating weather.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas prices soften on moderating weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices turned mostly softer Monday, led lower by milder weather forecasts in the eastern half of the U.S. later this week, industry sources said.
Gulf Coast prices slipped about five cents to the $2.70 per million British thermal units area, with the lower-priced deals evident in late trading.
At the Henry Hub, La., traders reported closing deals as high as $2.76 early but as low as the high-$2.60s shortly before nomination deadlines.
In the Midwest, swing prices fell another eight to 10 cents to the mid-to-high $2.50s, levels which were more in line with November 1 indices.
At the Chicago city-gate, traders reported closing deals in the low-to-mid $2.80s, down at least 10 cents from Friday.
Sources attributed the softening to milder temperatures now in many parts of the region, which are expected to seep into the remainder of the region later this week.
In west Texas, the drop in Midwest and Texas demand pushed Permian prices into the high-$2.50s to low-$2.60s, down more than five cents from Friday's level.
Normal to slightly above-normal temperatures are forecast to blanket Texas later this week and into the early part of next week, which may temper any significant rally to the upside, traders said.

At the southern California border, prices softened by an average of five cents to the mid-to-high $2.70s. However, a cooling trend is expected to arrive to the West Coast by the week's end, which may bring buyers, who are hesitant to tap into storage, back to the spot market.
At the New York city-gate, where a brief spell of cold has landed, prices fell at least 10 cents into the $3.05-3.10 area as slightly above-normal temperatures were expected by midweek.
